page.layout: One text column, full width. Above it, two round medallion engravings (coin portraits) side by side, each with a legend around the rim. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Gathering signature at the bottom right.

main_text.l: C. TIBERIUS. TIB. IMP. PATER
LIVIA. DRUSIL. MAT. TIB. IUN.
CL. TIBERIUS pater Tiberij Cæsaris, Quæstor sub C.
Cæsare, Alexandrino bello classi præpositus, plurimum ad vi-
ctoriam cōtulit: quare & pontifex in locum P. Scipionis substi-
tutus, & ad deducēdas in Galliā colonias, in queis Narbona
& Arelate erat, missus est. Cæsare occiso, cunctis turbarum metu
abolitione facta: decernentibus, etiā de præmiis tyrānicidarum
referendum cēsuit. Tandē indignē ferens nec statim se in con-
spectum Sexti Pompeij admissum, & fasciūm usu prohibitū, ad
M. Antonium traiecit in Achaiam: cum quo breui, reconciliata
inter omnes pace, Romam rediit, uxoremq; Liviam Drusillam,
& tunc grauidā, & antè iam apud se Tiberium enixam, peten-
ti Augusto concessit: nec multò post diem obiit, utroq; libero-
rum superstite, Tiberio, Drusoque Neronis. Sueto. in Tiber.
LIVIA Drusilla Cl. Tiberij supradicti uxor, Tiberij impe-
ratoris mater fuit, de qua dictū à nobis est in fine prioris partis
huius operis. hanc prægnantem abduxit Augustus: porrò qui
cōceptus erat, infans, immaturus est editus: is est Drusus Tibe-
rij Imperatoris frater minor natu, ac Claudij Cæsaris, qui Cali-
gulæ successit, pater: fuit alter Drusus Agrippinæ & Tibe. Impe,
filius. Cæterum in osculis Liviæ, & in hac voce defecit Augu-
stus, Livia nostra coniugi memor vive, ac vale.

page.notes: The two medallions are engravings; their rim legends are transcribed as printed text above, with u/v normalised and the partly hidden letters of the right-hand legend (LIVIA. DRVSIL. MAT. TIB. IVN.) read with some doubt. Doubtful: the Q of "Quæstor" has a stroke beneath it in the scan. "Sueto. in Tiber." is a marginal-style reference set within the text line. Running head and page number are as printed.
